```{ojs}
import {withDownload, cellFeatures, fmt, locatorMap, placeMarks, boxPolygon, pearson} from "../assets/js/dl.js"
S = FileAttachment("data/javamaize/summary.json").json()

countries = FileAttachment("data/javamaize/countries.geojson").json()
adm1 = FileAttachment("data/javamaize/adm1.geojson").json()
adm2 = FileAttachment("data/javamaize/adm2.geojson").json()
years = FileAttachment("data/javamaize/years.csv").csv({typed: true})
cells = FileAttachment("data/javamaize/cells.csv").csv({typed: true})
seasons = FileAttachment("data/javamaize/seasons.csv").csv({typed: true})
MASKS = ({spam: {label: "MapSPAM 2020 rice", col: "ha", what: "rice"},
          lg_all: {label: "LGRIP30 cropland", col: "ha_lgrip_all", what: "cropland"},
          lg_irr: {label: "LGRIP30 irrigated cropland", col: "ha_lgrip_irr", what: "irrigated cropland"}})
num = v => v != null && !Number.isNaN(v)
```

| Setup | |
|---|---|
| Area | 111.4-112.4 E, 8.0-7.0 S, East Java, on the rice fields of MapSPAM 2020 [@spam2020] |
| Crop map, for comparison | GFSAD [LGRIP30](https://doi.org/10.5067/Community/LGRIP/LGRIP30.001) cropland (30 m, nominal 2015), all or irrigated only: the same simulated cells, weighted by its cropland instead (the switch under the map) |
| Weather, soil | AgERA5 1990-2024 [@agera5]; SoilGrids 2.0 [@poggio2021], one profile per 0.1° cell |
| The sequence | one DSSAT crop sequence per cell (mode Q, template `XDRM8601.SQX`): IR 58 rice, 140 kg N/ha, transplanted on 15 November, then McCurdy 84aa maize, 120 kg N/ha, rainfed, sown on 15 March; the soil's water, nitrogen and organic matter pass from crop to crop. Two sequences: flooded rice, or rainfed rice behind a bund |
| The comparison | the same maize alone (template `XDMZ8201.MZX`), on the same cells and dates, each season starting from the soil profile at half its plant-available water |
| Years | 32 cycles, rice of 1991-2022 and maize of 1992-2023 |
| Boundaries | the Java case's province and district boundaries (BPS codes; see [Data, AOI, variety](../java/data.qmd)) |
| Experiment files | [`configs/cases/java-maize.yml`](https://github.com/bennyistanto/xdssat/blob/main/configs/cases/java-maize.yml), [`java-maize-alone.yml`](https://github.com/bennyistanto/xdssat/blob/main/configs/cases/java-maize-alone.yml) |

## Where

```{ojs}
md`The study box sits in East Java, the same island as the [main case study](../java/index.qmd).
${B.box_adm1.map((u, i) => `${u.name}${i === 0 ? " takes" : ""} ${fmt.pct(u.share_of_box)}${i === 0 ? " of it" : ""}`).join(", ")}.
Rice grows on ${fmt.int(S.ha)} ha of it (MapSPAM 2020), in ${S.cells} of the 0.1° weather cells: the fields where a
maize crop can follow the rice.`
```

The model runs on the 0.1° weather cells; every average and total on this page weights each cell by the
crop area inside it, not by the area of the cell. Which map gives that area is a choice. The switch below sets it
for every chart that weights by area: the rice fields of MapSPAM 2020 (the runs' own crop mask), or the
cropland of LGRIP30, all or irrigated only, for comparison. The simulated cells and their yields stay the same.

```{ojs}
viewof mask = Inputs.radio(new Map([["MapSPAM 2020 rice (the runs' crop mask)", "spam"], ["LGRIP30 cropland", "lg_all"],
  ["LGRIP30 irrigated cropland", "lg_irr"]]), {value: "spam", label: "Crop map"})
```

```{ojs}
wcol = MASKS[mask].col
wmean = (rows, k) => { const r = rows.filter(d => num(d[k]) && d[wcol] > 0); return d3.sum(r, d => d[k] * d[wcol]) / d3.sum(r, d => d[wcol]) }
place = cells
html`<div class="map-pair">
  ${withDownload(locatorMap(Plot, countries, B, {width: 280, height: 280}), "javamaize_locator", "red: the study box")}
  ${withDownload(Plot.plot({
    width: 420, height: 420,
    projection: {type: "equirectangular", domain: boxPolygon([B.box[0] - 0.05, B.box[1] - 0.05, B.box[2] + 0.05, B.box[3] + 0.05])},
    color: {scheme: "YlGn", legend: true, label: `${MASKS[mask].label} in the cell (ha)`},
    marks: [
      Plot.geo(cellFeatures(place), {fill: d => d.properties[wcol], stroke: "white", strokeWidth: 0.3}),
      ...placeMarks(Plot, adm1, adm2, {labels: "adm2"}),
      Plot.geo(boxPolygon(B.box), {stroke: "#d0021b", strokeWidth: 1.5, fill: "none"}),
      Plot.tip(place, Plot.pointer({x: "lon", y: "lat",
        title: d => `${Math.abs(d.lat).toFixed(2)} S, ${d.lon.toFixed(2)} E\nMapSPAM rice ${fmt.int(d.ha)} ha\n` +
          `LGRIP30 cropland ${fmt.int(d.ha_lgrip_all)} ha, irrigated ${fmt.int(d.ha_lgrip_irr)} ha`})),
      Plot.frame({stroke: "#bbb"})
    ]
  }), `javamaize_area_${mask}`, "0.1° cells; bold: provinces, thin: districts")}
</div>`
```

```{ojs}
maskTable = Object.entries(MASKS).map(([k, m]) => {
  const w = cells.filter(d => d[m.col] > 0)
  const wm = c => { const r = w.filter(d => num(d[c])); return d3.sum(r, d => d[c] * d[m.col]) / d3.sum(r, d => d[m.col]) }
  return {"Crop map": m.label + (k === mask ? " (selected)" : ""), "Area in the cells (ha)": d3.sum(cells, d => d[m.col]),
          "Correlation with MapSPAM, per cell": pearson(cells.map(d => d.ha), cells.map(d => d[m.col])),
          "Maize alone (kg/ha)": wm("maize_alone"), "Maize after flooded rice (kg/ha)": wm("maize_flooded"),
          "Gain (kg/ha)": wm("gain_flooded"),
          "Production, maize after flooded rice (Mt)": d3.sum(w.filter(d => num(d.maize_flooded)), d => d.maize_flooded * d[m.col]) / 1e9}
})
Inputs.table(maskTable, {format: {"Area in the cells (ha)": fmt.int, "Correlation with MapSPAM, per cell": fmt.d2,
  "Maize alone (kg/ha)": fmt.int, "Maize after flooded rice (kg/ha)": fmt.int, "Gain (kg/ha)": fmt.int,
  "Production, maize after flooded rice (Mt)": fmt.d1}, layout: "auto"})
```

```{ojs}
md`The map changes how much area there is far more than how much grows on it. LGRIP30 counts every cropland
pixel, of any crop, so its area is ${fmt.d1(maskTable[1]["Area in the cells (ha)"] / maskTable[0]["Area in the cells (ha)"])} times MapSPAM's
rice area (irrigated only: ${fmt.d1(maskTable[2]["Area in the cells (ha)"] / maskTable[0]["Area in the cells (ha)"])} times), and production follows. The
area-weighted yields move by ${fmt.pct(Math.abs(maskTable[1]["Maize alone (kg/ha)"] / maskTable[0]["Maize alone (kg/ha)"] - 1))} or less, because
each cell's yield comes from its weather and soil, and the map only decides how much each cell counts. Two
things the switch leaves out: a different map would also change the soil profiles (xdssat samples SoilGrids
under the crop pixels), and LGRIP30 is a single year (nominal 2015), as static as MapSPAM.`
```

## Two crops, one field

A single season, as DSSAT is usually run, starts from a soil the modeller describes: so much water, so much
nitrogen. A crop sequence starts only once. Every later crop inherits the soil the one before it left. DSSAT
does not carry the standing water: it sets the flood to zero at the start of every season
(`Paddy_Mgmt.for`, DSSAT-CSM 4.8). What carries is the soil itself.

The switch below picks the rice before the maize, for every chart on the page.

```{ojs}
viewof seq = Inputs.radio(new Map([["Flooded rice", "flooded"], ["Rainfed rice (bunded)", "rainfed"]]), {value: "flooded", label: "Rice"})
```

```{ojs}
md`Over the 32 cycles the ${seq} rice yields **${fmt.int(wmean(cells, `rice_${seq}`))} kg/ha** and is harvested a
median of ${fmt.int(d3.median(cells, d => d[`rice_days_${seq}`]))} days after transplanting, in February; at harvest its soil
holds **${fmt.int(wmean(cells, `rice_end_sw_${seq}`))} mm** of water the roots can still take up and
${fmt.int(wmean(cells, `rice_end_n_${seq}`))} kg/ha of mineral nitrogen. The maize sown on 15 March after it yields
**${fmt.int(wmean(cells, `maize_${seq}`))} kg/ha**; the same maize alone, starting from half the soil's available water,
**${fmt.int(wmean(cells, "maize_alone"))} kg/ha**. FAOSTAT puts Indonesia's national maize yield at 5.3-6.1 t/ha in
2018-2020 (<a href="#ref-faostat_qcl">FAO 2025</a>): the model's levels are higher; the comparison is the result.`
```

## The rice as insurance

```{ojs}
viewof dry = Inputs.range([250, 700], {value: 350, step: 10, label: "A dry maize season has less rain than (mm)"})
```

```{ojs}
weightOf = new Map(cells.map(d => [`${d.iy}_${d.ix}`, d[wcol]]))
yr = d3.groups(seasons, d => d.season_year).map(([y, rows]) => {
  const r = rows.map(d => ({...d, w: weightOf.get(`${d.iy}_${d.ix}`) || 0, after: d[`maize_${seq}`]}))
    .map(d => ({...d, gain: num(d.after) && num(d.maize_alone) ? d.after - d.maize_alone : NaN}))
  const wm = c => { const v = r.filter(d => num(d[c]) && d.w > 0); return d3.sum(v, d => d[c] * d.w) / d3.sum(v, d => d.w) }
  return {season_year: y, rain: wm("rain"), maize_alone: wm("maize_alone"), after: wm("after"), gain: wm("gain")}
}).sort((a, b) => a.season_year - b.season_year).map(d => ({...d, dryYear: d.rain < dry}))
dryRows = yr.filter(d => d.dryYear)
wetRows = yr.filter(d => !d.dryYear)
md`The gain is not spread evenly. In the **${dryRows.length}** seasons with less than ${dry} mm of rain between maize
sowing and maturity (area-weighted over the box), the maize after rice yields
**${fmt.int(d3.mean(dryRows, d => d.gain))} kg/ha** more than the maize alone; in the other ${wetRows.length} seasons,
**${fmt.int(d3.mean(wetRows, d => d.gain))} kg/ha** more. Across the years the gain falls as the rain rises
(correlation ${fmt.d2(pearson(yr.map(d => d.rain), yr.map(d => d.gain)))}). The water the rice leaves in
the soil is worth little when the maize gets rain of its own, and most when it does not: the first crop insures
the second.`
```

```{ojs}
withDownload(Plot.plot({
  height: 320, marginLeft: 60,
  x: {label: "Rain from maize sowing to maturity (mm, area-weighted)", grid: true},
  y: {label: "Maize after rice minus maize alone (kg/ha)", grid: true},
  color: {legend: true, domain: ["dry season", "other season"], range: ["#c0392b", "#2b6cb0"]},
  marks: [
    Plot.ruleX([dry], {stroke: "#c0392b", strokeDasharray: "4,3"}),
    Plot.ruleY([0]),
    Plot.dot(yr, {x: "rain", y: "gain", r: 5, fill: d => d.dryYear ? "dry season" : "other season", tip: true,
      title: d => `maize of ${d.season_year + 1} (after the rice of ${d.season_year})\nrain ${fmt.int(d.rain)} mm\n` +
        `alone ${fmt.int(d.maize_alone)}, after rice ${fmt.int(d.after)} kg/ha\ngain ${fmt.int(d.gain)} kg/ha`}),
    Plot.text(yr.filter(d => d.gain > 1500), {x: "rain", y: "gain", text: d => String(d.season_year + 1), dx: 18, fontSize: 10})
  ]
}), `javamaize_gain_vs_rain_${seq}_${mask}`, `one dot per maize season, weighted by ${MASKS[mask].label}`)
```

```{ojs}
barRows = yr.flatMap(d => [{year: d.season_year + 1, kind: "maize alone", kg: d.maize_alone, rain: d.rain},
                           {year: d.season_year + 1, kind: "maize after rice", kg: d.after, rain: d.rain}])
withDownload(Plot.plot({
  height: 300, marginLeft: 60,
  x: {label: null, tickFormat: d => String(d), ticks: 8},
  y: {label: "Maize yield (kg/ha)", grid: true},
  color: {legend: true, domain: ["maize alone", "maize after rice"], range: ["#c98b2b", "#2b8a3e"]},
  marks: [
    Plot.line(barRows, {x: "year", y: "kg", stroke: "kind", strokeWidth: 2}),
    Plot.dot(barRows, {x: "year", y: "kg", fill: "kind", r: 3, tip: true,
      title: d => `${d.year}, ${d.kind}\n${fmt.int(d.kg)} kg/ha\nmaize-season rain ${fmt.int(d.rain)} mm`}),
    Plot.ruleY([0])
  ]
}), `javamaize_maize_by_year_${seq}_${mask}`, `maize sown on 15 March of each year; weighted by ${MASKS[mask].label}`)
```

## What the sequence remembers

```{ojs}
soil = years.map(d => ({year: d.season_year, on: d[`soil_on_${seq}`], oc: d[`soil_oc_${seq}`], rice: d[`rice_${seq}`],
                        n: d[`rice_end_n_${seq}`]}))
s0 = soil[0]
s1 = soil[soil.length - 1]
md`A season run on its own forgets. A sequence does not, and over 32 cycles the model's field changes. With ${seq} rice,
the soil's organic nitrogen at rice harvest goes from **${fmt.int(s0.on)}** to **${fmt.int(s1.on)} kg/ha**
(${fmt.pct(s1.on / s0.on - 1)}), its organic carbon from ${fmt.int(s0.oc)} to ${fmt.int(s1.oc)} t/ha, and the rice yield
from ${fmt.int(d3.mean(soil.slice(0, 5), d => d.rice))} kg/ha in the first five cycles to
${fmt.int(d3.mean(soil.slice(-5), d => d.rice))} kg/ha in the last five, at the same 140 kg N. Two crops a year draw on
the soil's organic matter faster than the model returns it. A single-season run, which starts every year from
the same soil, cannot show this.`
```

```{ojs}
soilRows = soil.flatMap(d => [{year: d.year, what: "soil organic N (% of the first cycle)", v: d.on / s0.on, raw: `${fmt.int(d.on)} kg/ha`},
                              {year: d.year, what: "rice yield (% of the first cycle)", v: d.rice / s0.rice, raw: `${fmt.int(d.rice)} kg/ha`}])
withDownload(Plot.plot({
  height: 280, marginLeft: 60,
  x: {label: "Rice of", tickFormat: d => String(d), ticks: 8},
  y: {label: "Relative to the first cycle", tickFormat: "%", grid: true, domain: [0.4, 1.2]},
  color: {legend: true, domain: ["soil organic N (% of the first cycle)", "rice yield (% of the first cycle)"], range: ["#8c6d31", "#2b8a3e"]},
  marks: [
    Plot.ruleY([1], {stroke: "#999"}),
    Plot.line(soilRows, {x: "year", y: "v", stroke: "what", strokeWidth: 2}),
    Plot.dot(soilRows, {x: "year", y: "v", fill: "what", r: 2.5, tip: true, title: d => `${d.year}\n${d.what.split(" (")[0]}: ${d.raw}`})
  ]
}), `javamaize_soil_memory_${seq}`, "at rice harvest, weighted by MapSPAM 2020 rice (the crop map switch does not apply)")
```

## Cell by cell

```{ojs}
late = cells.filter(d => d[`rice_late_${seq}`] > 0)
md`In ${late.length} cell${late.length === 1 ? "" : "s"}, the ${seq} rice is still in the field on 15 March in at least one cycle
${late.length ? `(in ${late.filter(d => d[`rice_late_${seq}`] >= 0.99).length} of them every cycle)` : ""}. DSSAT then sows the maize
on the next 15 March, a year late, and the sequence slips. xdssat labels each crop by its sowing date, so those
maize seasons are left out of the comparison rather than paired with the wrong rice.`
```

```{ojs}
viewof mapMetric = Inputs.radio(new Map([["Gain of maize after rice", `gain_${seq}`], ["Maize alone", "maize_alone"],
  ["Maize after rice", `maize_${seq}`], ["Years with a gain", "share_gain"], ["Rice still in the field on 15 March", `rice_late_${seq}`]]),
  {value: `gain_${seq}`, label: "Map"})
```

```{ojs}
withDownload(Plot.plot({
  height: 460, aspectRatio: 1,

  color: {scheme: mapMetric.startsWith("gain") ? "Greens" : mapMetric.startsWith("rice_late") ? "Reds" : "YlGn", legend: true,
          tickFormat: (mapMetric === "share_gain" || mapMetric.startsWith("rice_late")) ? "%" : undefined,
          label: mapMetric.startsWith("gain") ? "Maize after rice minus alone (kg/ha)" : mapMetric === "share_gain" ?
                 "Share of seasons with a gain (flooded rice)" : mapMetric.startsWith("rice_late") ? "Share of cycles" : "Maize yield (kg/ha)"},
  marks: [
    Plot.geo(cellFeatures(cells), {fill: d => d.properties[mapMetric], stroke: "white", strokeWidth: 0.4}),
    ...placeMarks(Plot, adm1, adm2, {labels: "adm2", fontSize: 9}),
    Plot.tip(cells, Plot.pointer({x: "lon", y: "lat",
      title: d => `${Math.abs(d.lat).toFixed(2)} S, ${d.lon.toFixed(2)} E\nmaize alone ${fmt.int(d.maize_alone)}, after ${seq} rice ` +
        `${fmt.int(d[`maize_${seq}`])} kg/ha\nrice ${fmt.int(d[`rice_${seq}`])} kg/ha, harvested after ${fmt.int(d[`rice_days_${seq}`])} days\n` +
        `rice ${fmt.int(d.ha)} ha`})),
    Plot.frame()
  ]
}), `javamaize_cell_map_${seq}`, "mean of 32 cycles per 0.1° cell")
```

## Checked against district statistics

The Ministry of Agriculture's statistics portal (BDSP) gives every district's maize harvested area,
production and yield each year [@bdsp_jagung], as it does for the rice of the
[main case study](../java/index.qmd). Every weather cell goes to the district that holds its centre.

```{ojs}
obs = FileAttachment("data/javamaize/observed.csv").csv({typed: true})
obsD = FileAttachment("data/javamaize/observed_districts.csv").csv({typed: true})
O = S.observed
md`Over ${O.years[0]}-${O.years[1]} the ${O.districts} districts of the box harvested a mean
**${fmt.int(d3.mean(obs, d => d.obs))} kg/ha** of maize (production over harvested area, as reported); the model's maize
after ${seq} rice gives **${fmt.int(d3.mean(obs, d => d[`maize_${seq}`]))} kg/ha**, ${fmt.d1(d3.mean(obs, d => d[`maize_${seq}`]) / d3.mean(obs, d => d.obs))}
times as much. The years do not agree either: after removing each series' trend, their correlation is
**${fmt.d2(O.r_detrended[`maize_${seq}`])}** (maize alone: ${fmt.d2(O.r_detrended.maize_alone)}). The statistics count all of a district's maize, in every season and on every field; the model grows
one dry-season crop on the rice fields, uncalibrated. The dry years in which the rice
insures the maize in the model leave no mark in the district totals. Before the model's numbers say anything
about a real harvest, it needs maize statistics of the dry season on rice fields, or field trials, to be
calibrated against.`
```

```{ojs}
obsRows = obs.flatMap(d => [{year: d.year, kind: "district statistics (BDSP)", kg: d.obs},
                            {year: d.year, kind: `model, maize after ${seq} rice`, kg: d[`maize_${seq}`]},
                            {year: d.year, kind: "model, maize alone", kg: d.maize_alone}])
withDownload(Plot.plot({
  height: 300, marginLeft: 60,
  x: {label: "Harvest year", tickFormat: d => String(d), ticks: 8},
  y: {label: "Maize yield (kg/ha)", grid: true, domain: [0, d3.max(obsRows, d => d.kg) * 1.05]},
  color: {legend: true, domain: ["district statistics (BDSP)", `model, maize after ${seq} rice`, "model, maize alone"],
          range: ["#222", "#2b8a3e", "#c98b2b"]},
  marks: [
    Plot.line(obsRows, {x: "year", y: "kg", stroke: "kind", strokeWidth: 2}),
    Plot.dot(obsRows, {x: "year", y: "kg", fill: "kind", r: 2.5, tip: true,
      title: d => `${d.year}\n${d.kind}: ${fmt.int(d.kg)} kg/ha`}),
    Plot.ruleY([0])
  ]
}), `javamaize_observed_${seq}`, "statistics: total production over total harvested area of the districts; model: weighted by MapSPAM 2020 rice over their cells (the crop map switch does not apply)")
```

## What this does not say

- **Simulated, not observed.** Why the simulated yields differ from official statistics, in every case study:
  [FAQ](../about/faq.qmd#why-do-the-simulated-yields-differ-from-the-official-statistics).
- **Uncalibrated, and borrowed cultivars.** IR 58 comes from the IRRI experiment behind the rice template and
  McCurdy 84aa from the Florida experiment behind the maize template, with DSSAT's own coefficients and
  without pests, diseases or weeds. Neither is an East Javan variety.
- **Fixed dates.** The rice is transplanted on 15 November and the maize sown on 15 March in every cell and
  year, whatever the rain or the rice harvest; farmers decide each season.
- **The comparison's starting point.** "Maize alone" starts at half the soil's available water, an assumption.
  Another starting point would move its yield, and so the gain; the sequence needs no such assumption.
- **The soil's slow change** depends on what the template returns to the field after each harvest and on the
  SoilGrids organic carbon the run starts from; it is the model's trend, not a measured one.

## Run it yourself

```bash
python scripts/prepare_weather.py   --config configs/cases/java-maize.yml
python scripts/prepare_crop_mask.py --config configs/cases/java-maize.yml
python scripts/prepare_soils.py     --config configs/cases/java-maize.yml --aoi java_maize_case
python scripts/run_aoi.py --config configs/cases/java-maize.yml --regime irrigated
python scripts/run_aoi.py --config configs/cases/java-maize.yml --regime rainfed
python scripts/run_aoi.py --config configs/cases/java-maize-alone.yml
python scripts/fetch_bdsp.py --komoditas JAGUNG --prov 33 35        # district maize statistics
python docs/scripts/export_cases.py javamaize
python docs/scripts/export_boundaries.py javamaize
```
